applies_to: easYgen-3100XT-P1 / 3200XT-P1 / 3200XT-P1-LT, release 2.17-0, default Modbus data protocol 5010 (Basic Visualization).
summary: The easYgen-3000XT is Woodward's genset controller for standby, AMF, peak-shaving and mains-parallel plants. It is a Modbus RTU slave on RS-485 and a Modbus TCP server on Ethernet. Measurements, status and alarm flags are read from a fixed telegram (protocol 5010) starting at address 50000; remote start/stop, acknowledge and interface setpoints are written to parameter addresses 503-511. This page covers generator, mains and engine values, the main status and alarm words, and the remote-control words.

addressing.note: The protocol 5010 table in the appendix prints wire addresses (Protocol ID at 50000). The Modbus chapter shows the same block Modicon-style from 450001 and says 450001 can become bus address 50000. Parameters (remote control, setpoints) use Modicon address = 40000 + (parameter ID + 1), so parameter 503 is 40504 and wire address 503. The manual warns some PC tools need a shift of one (e.g. 504); if a write has no effect, try the neighbour.

source.title: Manual easYgen-3000XT Series Genset Control, Release 2.17-0
source.pages: pp. 632-633 (RS-485 / Modbus settings), 676 (Modbus/TCP slave ID), 760-761 and 844-848 (remote control via Modbus), 919-922 (Modbus address ranges, data types), 987-1024 (protocol 5010 table), 1147-1152 (remote control words and interface setpoints)

notes: The manual states Modbus registers are big-endian; 32-bit values are read high word first (ABCD). LogicsManager composite parameters are the exception (little-endian) and are not on this page.

Left out: the 16-bit power, voltage and current values at 50010-50021 and 50031-50040. Their scale depends on exponents published at 50001-50003 and the manual does not give the formula clearly enough; use the 32-bit values from 50322, which have fixed scaling.

Left out: 50028/50029 (setpoint frequency / PF, printed with a multiplier of 1 that does not fit their units), the 'active (reserved)' alarm words, and rows the table marks for the easYgen-3400XT/3500XT only (busbar L2-L3/L3-L1, LSx values, GGB bits, analog inputs 4-12, relays 13-22).
The status message at 50100 is an index into the manual's status message list; the index-to-text mapping is not tabulated, so no enum is given.
'Latched' alarm words hold an alarm until it is acknowledged. The controller also offers alarm telegrams (protocols 5011/5017) that are not covered here.

Interface setpoints only take effect when the matching AnalogManager source (05.56, 05.12, 05.53, 05.59, 05.83) is selected. Parameters 507-511 are described with CANopen object data types; their Modbus addresses follow the parameter rule on p. 921.
The easYgen-3400XT/3500XT use the same 5010 telegram but are documented in their own manual, which was not checked for this page.
The parameter list gives Ethernet A a default IP of 10.31.140.0 with mask 255.255.240.0. The TCP port is not stated in the manual.

integration.summary: Block-read holding registers from 50000 (up to 128 per request) for status and alarms, and the 32-bit generator and mains values at 50322-50411. To start or stop the set, write parameter 503 with 0 and then the start (bit 0) or stop (bit 1) bit; acknowledge alarms by pulsing bit 4 twice.
integration.enable: RS-485: set Modbus slave ID (parameter 3188, default 1; 0 disables Modbus) and baud/parity/stop bits (3170-3172). Ethernet: set Modbus/TCP slave ID (7485) and the Ethernet A IP settings, then turn on the matching 'Set IP address' parameter. Protocol number 3184 must stay 5010 for this map; a change needs a reboot. For a remote start, the LogicsManager start request must include 04.13 Remote request.
integration.watchdog: No Modbus communication timeout is documented. Bits 2 and 3 of parameter 503 must always be 0; the manual reserves them for a watchdog. A remote start request (04.13) stays set until a stop bit arrives or power is lost.
quirks: Start, stop and acknowledge act on rising edges: write 0, then the bit. Writing the same value again does nothing.
Acknowledge needs two rising edges of bit 4: the first silences the horn, the second resets alarms that are no longer active.
Status-word bit numbers here follow the manual's masks: mask 8000h = bit 15.
Reads use function 03; parameters are written with 06 or 16. Parameters are accessed one at a time, with a length that matches their data type.
Some PC tools need the address shifted by one (e.g. 504 instead of 503); the manual says to try both.

Each parameter ID has its own address, and a 32-bit parameter is read or written as 2 registers starting at that address (high word first). So 507 (INT32) is sent as 507+508 in one request, yet 508 alone is the separate PF setpoint; likewise 510 and 511. Never block-read or block-write across 503-511; send one request per parameter with the length of its data type.
setup: RS-485 defaults: 19.2 kBd, no parity, one stop bit, full-duplex mode (parameter 3173). Select half-duplex for a two-wire bus and set a reply delay (3189) if the master needs it.
Modbus/TCP: up to 5 sockets. An idle socket closes after about 2.2 s and opening one takes about 200 ms, so poll continuously or expect reconnects.
The manual recommends a 10 ms pause after each response; RTU replies can take up to 2-3 s on display / plastic-housing units.
gotchas: This controller starts engines and closes breakers. Make sure the site is safe and the operators know before writing parameter 503.

Bit 9 of parameter 503 sets 03.40 Remote Shutdown. One chapter says it shuts the engine down at once, but the configuration chapters route 03.40 through a LogicsManager flag and a free alarm with a shutdown class. Check how your unit is set up before relying on it.
Writing setpoints 507-511 changes nothing until the AnalogManager setpoint source points at the interface value.
Password protection for Modbus RS-485 (9128) and Ethernet (9129) defaults to On. The manual says the remote-control words and interface setpoints need no password; parameter changes do.

address_note: address = 0-based Modbus wire (PDU) address; documented = as printed in the source.
